critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2226-L2296 (/diag/wardrobe-scan) — good defensive design: masks emails, excludes item names/photos, aggregates via read-only pipeline, never issues any write. Backed by an explicit no-writes test.

server.py L167-L196 (get_scope) — is_primary computed as `primary[0]['id'] == prof['id']` where primary is the earliest-created profile per user_id. Correct as long as profile creation timestamps are stable and unique; if two profiles ever share created_at, the winner is undefined (edge case, unlikely). Consider tie-breaking on id.

server.py L244-L253 (enforce_limit) — premium account on a secondary wardrobe hits the '/main wardrobe/' branch ONLY for non-metered features (cfg is None). Metered features (dressme, stylist) still increment usage against the account_id; that's the correct behaviour per spec.
server.py L1380-L1390 (create_item) — free-cap uses `not user.get('account_premium')` so a premium household's secondary wardrobes are UNCAPPED. Verified.

frontend/app/bulk-add.tsx — clean: no auto-picker useEffect, try/catch/finally-equivalent semantics via setOpening(false) before the error branches and busy.current=false in every terminal path (cancel L42, post-loop L97). Diag stages logged as required.
frontend/app/audit.tsx L36-L45 (runScan) — sets scanning true before the call and false after, timeoutMs 60000, error path renders through the existing error box. Simple and correct.
frontend/src/components/WardrobeSwitcher.tsx L80-L82 — copy explicitly says 'not separate Premium seats' and 'kept completely separate' — matches the spec that Premium is not household-wide.
